title: Nūn Sākinah, Tanwīn and Mīm Sākinah
titleArabic: أحكام النون الساكنة والتنوين والميم الساكنة

sections.title: Mīm Sākinah
sections.hint: A mīm with no vowel. Before another mīm it merges and hums (idghām shafawī); before ب it is hidden with a hum (ikhfāʾ shafawī); before every other letter it is said clearly (iẕhār shafawī). First, because iqlāb below turns a nūn into exactly this mīm.

sections.title: Iẕhār Ḥalqī
sections.hint: Before the six throat letters — ء ه ع ح غ خ — the nūn sākinah or tanwīn is said clearly, with no hum. The tanwīn is written stacked.

sections.title: Idghām bi-Ghunnah
sections.hint: Before ي ن م و the nūn or tanwīn merges into the next letter and the hum stays — two harakat of ghunna on the merged letter.

sections.title: Idghām bilā Ghunnah
sections.hint: Before ل and ر the nūn or tanwīn merges completely — a doubled letter with no hum at all.

sections.title: Ikhfāʾ Ḥaqīqī
sections.hint: Before the fifteen remaining letters the nūn is hidden: the tongue does not touch, and only the hum is heard — two harakat — while the mouth shapes the next letter. The tanwīn is written staggered. صِفۡ ذَا ثَنَا كَمۡ جَادَ شَخۡصٌ قَدۡ سَمَا  •  دُمۡ طَيِّبًا زِدۡ فِي تُقًى ضَعۡ ظَالِمَا

sections.title: Iqlāb
sections.hint: Before ب the nūn sākinah or tanwīn turns into a hidden mīm with a hum. The Mushaf writes a small mīm in place of the sukoon, and the tanwīn gives up one of its two marks for it.
